title: Review: jmap-mail-server crate
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — onSuccessUpdateEmail is completely broken (silent no-op on updates). collapseThreads is an OOM vector. These are the two highest-risk items. Other findings are edge cases or cosmetic.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: the onSuccessUpdateEmail extra-invocation format question depends on how jmap-server's Dispatcher handles extra invocations — I haven't read that crate. If the dispatcher appends extra invocations verbatim (not re-executing them), submission.rs is right and email.rs/copy is wrong. Would raise confidence if: read jmap-server dispatcher source. Uncertainty driven by: Invocation type dual-use (request and response have same shape), dispatcher behavior not visible from this crate.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — The code is mostly idiomatic Rust. Ownership is handled correctly throughout; no gratuitous Arc or Rc usage. Error handling uses the ? operator appropriately. The three clippy-level findings (redundant clone, unwrap_or instead of continue, SetError non_exhaustive) are all fixable without architectural changes. The SetErrorType::Display via serde roundtrip is the worst idiom issue and is already filed.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: I may have missed iterator-vs-loop patterns in longer match arms in submission.rs. Uncertainty driven by: focused primarily on semantic bugs in the first pass and may have glossed over small idiom issues in submission.rs's longer functions.
